pathway.title: Bally's Corp — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is high on every measure available and rests on a non-GAAP earnings measure. Total debt of USD 4,910.1 million is 9.57x last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 512.8 million, and net of unrestricted cash of USD 390.2 million it is 8.81x [CP-1 leverage chart data]. The ratio rose from 8.88x at September 30, 2025, although the intervening perimeter changes mean it is indicative rather than like-for-like [CP-1 Financial base view]. Operating lease liabilities of USD 2,392.3 million sit outside this debt figure and the fixed rent is deducted inside Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1 financials table].

Cash earnings are almost fully absorbed by financing and rent. Cash interest of USD 444.6 million is 86.7% of Adjusted EBITDA, so Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 1.15x. Adding the triple net rent expense of USD 210.0 million to cash interest, Adjusted EBITDAR of USD 722.8 million covers the total 1.10x. The 2026 term loans cost at least USD 105.4 million a year even at the 3.0% floor plus the lower 6.5% base-rate margin, and more under the 7.5% Term SOFR margin, and part of the interest may be paid in kind [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 335.7 million over the last twelve months [CP-1 financials table].

Liquidity is the decisive issue. Cash of USD 390.2 million and reported revolver availability of USD 195.8 million total USD 586.0 million, compared with a six-month free cash outflow (operating cash flow less capital expenditures and capitalized software) of USD 359.1 million [CP-1 liquidity chart data; Q2 2026 10-Q page:5]. Revolver commitments are due to fall to about USD 319 million from October 2026 while USD 303.75 million is drawn, which leaves essentially no headroom once the reduction applies, before other usage of USD 19.75 million that CP-1 could not explain [Q2 2026 10-Q page:33]. Whether the reduction occurred, and how it was met, is Not supplied because the pack ends at August 14, 2026.

Covenant protection exists only through a conditional waiver. In May 2026 the required lenders conditionally waived the consolidated net leverage ratio covenant for each quarter from March 31, 2026 until the earlier of the company’s election or the day before the compliance certificate for the quarter ending March 31, 2027, subject to minimum liquidity, limits on additional secured debt and an agreement to amend the revolver [Q2 2026 10-Q page:38]. The company states that it does not project that it would satisfy the liquidity maintenance requirement or the reinstated covenant absent the financings under discussion, and that substantial doubt about going concern exists [Q2 2026 10-Q page:11]. The waiver level and the reported ratio are Not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable.

The structure divides the debt across two borrower groups. Parent-group debt is USD 2,898.3 million: USD 1,413.3 million of first lien revolver and 2026 term loans and USD 1,485.0 million of senior notes. Bally’s Intralot debt is USD 2,011.8 million, and Bally’s Intralot does not guarantee the parent’s debt [CP-1 debt table; CP-1A Transaction summary]. The two Intralot-linked segments produced USD 86.7 million of Q2 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDAR, leaving USD 37.4 million of Adjusted EBITDA from casinos, North America Interactive and corporate cost after rent [Q2 2026 10-Q page:48]. The mapping of segments to legal entities is not supplied, so parent-level leverage is only indicative; on this basis it is about 19.4x annualized Q2 2026 and 23.8x last twelve months.

Earnings quality is limited by add-backs and by margin pressure. Add-backs for transaction, development, merger, share-based and other items were USD 106.4 million in the six months to June 30, 2026, 43.0% of Adjusted EBITDA of USD 247.3 million [Q2 2026 10-Q page:48]. Q2 2026 revenue rose to USD 792.2 million while Adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 124.0 million from USD 129.2 million, with gaming expenses at 52% of gaming revenue against 43% a year earlier [CP-1 segment base; CP-1A operating model].

Maturities are light until 2029 but the revolver and the 2029 wall matter. Debt maturing through 2027 is USD 141.4 million, 2028 is USD 282.3 million and 2029 is USD 1,007.0 million; the USD 1,109.5 million of 2026 term loans fall due in 2029 instead of 2031 if the 2029 Notes are still outstanding then, which would lift the 2029 amount to USD 2,116.5 million [CP-1 maturities chart data]. Refinancing of the 2029 Notes is therefore linked to the secured term loan maturity.

runs.text: Strength, Documentary Fact: a diversified, licensed operating base. The company runs 19 US land-based casinos, a large online gaming business and a lottery technology business, with no customer above 10% of revenue, and holds Rhode Island master contracts to 2043, a New York gaming license and a Chicago development [CP-1A Company and operating model; Company profile]. This supports revenue durability, although segment cash earnings are not evenly distributed.

Strength, Documentary Fact: lender engagement and external funding for part of the capital programme. Lenders granted a waiver and amended the revolver in 2026, and GLPI has committed to advance up to USD 940.0 million for Chicago construction, which reduces the company’s own capital need there [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Lender engagement lowers near-term acceleration risk but does not remove the conditions.

Strength, Documentary Fact: contained near-term amortisation. Remaining 2026 and 2027 maturities total USD 141.4 million, and a parent revolver default has no implications under Bally’s Intralot’s debt documents [CP-1 maturities chart data; Q2 2026 10-Q page:11]. This limits contagion from a parent-level default to the Intralot group.

Strength, Analyst Interpretation: real estate and asset monetisation capacity. The Bally’s Twin River sale-leaseback realised USD 700.0 million of consideration, and the company lists asset monetisation among its plans [CP-1A Transaction summary]. This is also a weakness because each sale adds fixed rent, so I count it only as a source of liquidity, not of lower fixed charges.

Weakness, Documentary Fact: leverage and cover. Gross leverage of 9.57x, net leverage of 8.81x and cover of 1.15x leave little cushion, and the fixed-charge cover including rent is 1.10x [CP-1 charts; calculations below].

Weakness, Documentary Fact: liquidity and going concern. Operating cash flow is negative, cash fell from USD 798.4 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 390.2 million at June 30, 2026, and the latest filing states substantial doubt [CP-1 liquidity chart data; CP-1A Company profile].

Weakness, Analyst Interpretation: structure and control. A controlling sponsor holds 67.1%, no equity support is documented, parent creditors rank behind Intralot creditors at the Intralot level, and 42.1% of Intralot equity belongs to others [CP-1A Company profile; Governance]. The sponsor’s response is the key unknown.

Weakness, Documentary Fact: reporting quality and regulation. The 10-K reports an adverse opinion on internal control because of a material weakness, results were first issued as preliminary, and the Rhode Island regulatory agreement restricts payments and debt incurrence above a 5.50 to 1.00 leverage trigger whose definition and status are not supplied [CP-1A Company profile].

Weakness, Documentary Fact: uncommitted large projects. The USD 4.0 billion Bally’s Bronx project has a non-binding loan term sheet and a letter of intent with a potential equity investor, and construction at Chicago continues [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Funding competes with debt service.

cells.text: Bally’s Corporation, a Delaware corporation, global headquarters in Providence, Rhode Island; common stock on the NYSE under BALY.
Country: United States. Context lists the sector as Hotels & Motels; that label is a run setting, not issuer evidence.

A global gaming, hospitality, entertainment and technology company with 20 casinos globally, including in the UK and 11 US states, a golf course in New York and horse racetracks, Bally Bet, and a majority interest in Bally’s Intralot (active in 39 jurisdictions).
The Q2-26 release says 20 casinos in 11 US states and one in Newcastle (page:6); see conflicts.
Standard General, the largest shareholder, beneficially owned 67.1% of common stock as of February 28, 2026; at the merger date Parent and affiliates beneficially owned 73.8%.
The percentages are at different dates and are not reconciled; the change is not explained in the pages read.
Standard General’s Managing Partner and Chief Investment Officer is Executive Chairman; the company is a controlled company under NYSE standards, not required to follow certain governance rules.
Concentrated control can support or extract; sources show no equity support and no distribution to the sponsor in the pages read.
Bally’s Intralot (57.9% owned, 42.1% non-controlling interest, listed in Athens as BYLOT); Bally’s Chicago, Inc. sold equity to local and accredited investors in 2025.
Non-controlling interest was 1,525,228 thousand at June 30, 2026 (CP-1). A Bally’s Intralot dividend of 17,644 thousand was declared in Q2 2026 and paid on July 27, 2026 (Q2-26 10-Q page:4, page:13).

37.7% equity interest in The Star Entertainment Group Limited, held under the fair value option; 19.99% interest in an unconsolidated entity that holds a carved-out business, which pays licence fees through a trust.
The fair value change is a non-cash item of 139,590 thousand in the six-month cash flow reconciliation (page:5), so investment value is volatile and reaches net loss.
11,619,725 penny warrants and 2,897,120 outstanding awards could add shares; 48,988,040 shares were outstanding at June 30, 2026.
Warrants issued under the Sinclair Framework Agreement (10-K page:127).

Amended and Restated Regulatory Agreement with Rhode Island regulators: restricts restricted payments, additional indebtedness and other actions if the leverage ratio exceeds 5.50 to 1.00 (gross debt divided by Adjusted EBITDA, each as defined there); master contracts run to June 30, 2043 with a 100 million investment commitment.

The regulatory definition is not supplied. The ratios in CP-1 use different definitions and are not a measure of compliance, but the 5.50 to 1.00 trigger sits well below the CP-1 gross leverage of 9.57x. The effect on the company is therefore a gap CP-2 must open.

The 10-K reports an adverse opinion on internal control because of a material weakness; the March 16, 2026 release announced preliminary results with a 10-K extension, and the 10-K is dated March 23, 2026.
The 10-K risk factor summary says "material weaknesses" while the body says "a material weakness" (10-K page:20, page:51).
The auditor states it has served since 2015.
The auditor issued an unqualified opinion on the financial statements (10-K page:194).
Management says Bally’s has over 12,000 employees.
Q2-26 10-Q states conditions "raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern"; management’s plans do not alleviate it.
First appearance in the pack; not in the 10-K or the Q1-26 10-Q.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The February 7, 2025 merger. Bally’s completed merger transactions with SG Parent LLC and The Queen Casino & Entertainment, Inc., an affiliate of Parent (10-K page:7). Public holders received $18.25 per share in cash, Parent and its affiliates then beneficially owned 73.8% of the common stock, and Queen became a wholly owned subsidiary (Q2-26 10-Q page:8). Share repurchases of 22,804,384 shares for 416,180 thousand in the Successor period to June 30, 2025 equal the number of shares multiplied by $18.25 (Q2-26 10-Q page:4, page:5; calculation below), which is consistent with the cash consideration; I read it as Analyst Interpretation because the filing does not label the repurchase that way in the pages read. Non-cash consideration issued was 955,647 thousand for the company merger and 555,751 thousand for the Queen merger (Q2-26 10-Q page:6). At closing the company issued $500 million of 11% first lien senior secured notes due October 2, 2028 under a note purchase agreement (10-K page:85); the use of proceeds is not stated in the pages read, so whether any distribution was debt-funded is Insufficient Information. The notes were repaid in October 2025: Intralot transaction proceeds first paid down 500.0 million of secured debt pro rata across the 2028 Notes and the Term Loan Facility, then an additional payment of 395.0 million settled the remaining 2028 Notes, with a make-whole payment (10-K page:87).

The Intralot transaction. On October 8, 2025 Bally’s completed the transaction under the July 18, 2025 agreement: Intralot paid $1.8 billion in cash and issued about 873.7 million shares for all of Bally’s Holdings Limited, which held the International Interactive business, and Bally’s ownership rose to a controlling 57.9% (Q2-26 10-Q page:8). It was accounted for as an equity transaction with a 42.1% non-controlling interest and no gain or loss (Q2-26 10-Q page:8). Bally’s assumed Intralot debt of about $1.97 billion principal (10-K page:166). Intralot Capital Luxembourg S.A. is the main borrower: a 400.0 million pound term loan, a 200.0 million euro Greek term loan, a super senior revolver with 160.0 million euros of commitments, 600.0 million euros of 6.75% fixed notes and 300.0 million euros of floating notes (Q2-26 10-Q page:31 to page:37). Parent group debt is not guaranteed by Bally’s Intralot, and Bally’s Intralot debt carries its own covenants (a total net leverage ratio not exceeding 4.75:1.00) (Q2-26 10-Q page:11, page:38).

The 2026 refinancing and sale-leaseback. On February 11, 2026 the company entered into $1.1 billion of senior secured 2026 Term Loans: Term SOFR (3.0% floor) plus 7.5%, with up to 3.5% payable in kind, secured pari passu with the revolver, due February 11, 2031, or March 1, 2029 if the 2029 Notes remain outstanding on that date (Q2-26 10-Q page:34, page:32). It repaid the previous Term Loan Facility in full, paying $1.48 billion and recognising a $63.4 million loss on extinguishment (Q2-26 10-Q page:33). The same day it sold the Bally’s Twin River land and real estate to GLPI for total consideration of $700.0 million, leased it back under Master Lease No. 2, and agreed 56.0 million of added annual rent; it recorded a gain of $105.8 million (Q2-26 10-Q page:39). Revolver commitments fell by 22.5% to about $519.3 million, with the revolver maturity split into October 2026 and October 2028 tranches and total availability falling to about $319 million from October 2026 (Q2-26 10-Q page:33, page:66). A revolver drawing of $448.0 million made in January 2026 for the New York license fee was repaid in February 2026 (Q2-26 10-Q page:66).

Covenant relief and amendments. In May 2026 the required revolving lenders conditionally waived compliance with the consolidated net leverage ratio covenant from the quarter ended March 31, 2026 until the earlier of the company’s certification election or the day before delivery of the compliance certificate for the quarter ending March 31, 2027; the waiver is conditioned on minimum liquidity, limits on additional secured debt and an agreement to amend the revolver (Q2-26 10-Q page:38). A Fourth Amendment dated May 5, 2026 raised revolver margins (Q2-26 10-Q page:64, page:74); a Fifth Amendment dated July 29, 2026 is listed as incorporated from a Form 8-K of August 5, 2026 whose terms are Not supplied (Q2-26 10-Q page:74). The Q2-26 10-Q states the company does not project that it would satisfy the liquidity maintenance requirement or the reinstated covenant over the next twelve months absent the financings under discussion (page:11).

Development and licence commitments. The company was awarded a New York downstate gaming license in December 2025 and paid the $500.0 million license fee in the first quarter of 2026, plus a $115 million golf course concession contingent payment (Q2-26 10-Q page:44; Q2-26 release page:2). A conveyance arrangement recorded a liability of $183.6 million for specified capital improvements (Q2-26 10-Q page:25), with improvements of approximately $161.0 million required (page:44). The Bronx project is described as a $4.0 billion integrated casino project expected to open by 2030 (Q2-26 release page:2, management language), and a bond or cash deposit equal to 5% of total project investment is required (Q2-26 10-Q page:44). Chicago: the permanent casino targets opening in early 2027 on management’s account (Q2-26 release page:2); GLPI has committed to advance up to $940.0 million of hard costs in exchange for added rent of 8.5% of advances, on top of 20.0 million initial annual rent (Q2-26 10-Q page:70). In the Las Vegas site, the Athletics stadium is slated for completion before the 2028 season (Q2-26 release page:2).

Investments and acquisitions. In April 2025 the company committed A$200 million in convertible notes and subordinated debt for an approximately 38% economic interest in The Star Entertainment Group Limited (10-K page:6); it now holds a 37.7% equity interest (Q2-26 10-Q page:15). Bally’s Intralot agreed in June 2026 to acquire evoke plc, with a cooperation agreement dated June 5, 2026 (Q2-26 release page:1; Q2-26 10-Q page:74). The consideration, financing and approvals timetable are Not supplied; since the buyer is Bally’s Intralot, which does not guarantee parent debt, any financing sits with the Intralot group unless otherwise documented, which is an Analyst Interpretation. Bally’s Intralot also signed a total return equity swap on June 15, 2026 over its own shares for up to 50.0 million euros (Q2-26 10-Q page:28).

Subsequent events and new debt after the quarter. Bally’s Intralot, through Intralot Capital, signed a sterling term facilities agreement for 261.8 million pounds on July 27, 2026, drawn in two three-year tranches (Q2-26 10-Q page:37). In July 2026 the company signed a non-binding term sheet for a loan to fund the Bally’s Bronx project and general corporate purposes (Q2-26 10-Q page:11), and in August 2026 a letter of intent with a potential equity investor (Q2-26 release page:2, management language). No later event is supplied.

Debt, cash, maturities, cash paid for interest, Adjusted EBITDA and its reconciliation are all printed in filed documents, so the ratios below are calculated only from printed figures. The ratios are not like-for-like across dates. Reported 2025 amounts are split at the February 7, 2025 merger, so each last-twelve-month figure is a sum of a Predecessor stub and Successor periods. The Intralot group debt entered the balance sheet in the fourth quarter of 2025 and is counted in full at each later date, while the Intralot B2B earnings count only from October 8, 2025, so leverage at the later dates is higher than a pro forma view would show; the sources do not provide that view. Adjusted EBITDA is after cash rent on triple net operating leases, so operating lease liabilities are excluded from debt for consistency, and are shown separately. The June 30, 2026 liquidity position and the unfinished financing plans described in the going concern note are the main credit issue; the ratios describe the burden, not the headroom under any covenant, because the covenant definitions are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Bally’s Corporation is a Providence, Rhode Island based operator that the 10-K describes as a global gaming, hospitality, entertainment and technology company. Since February 2025 it has been rebuilt by three transactions: the February 7, 2025 merger with entities affiliated with Standard General and The Queen Casino & Entertainment, Inc.; the October 8, 2025 combination of its International Interactive business with Intralot, which left Bally’s with 57.9% of Bally’s Intralot; and, in 2026, a refinancing and sale-leaseback programme. The business has four reportable segments: Casinos & Resorts, Bally’s Intralot B2B (lottery technology), Bally’s Intralot B2C (online gaming, mainly the UK) and North America Interactive. For a creditor, the structure matters more than the segment mix: ownership is concentrated in one sponsor, the largest growth businesses sit in a subsidiary with its own non-guaranteeing debt group, most casino real estate is leased from GLPI, and two large development projects need capital: Chicago, partly funded by GLPI advances of up to 940.0 million, and the Bronx, whose funding beyond the license fee is not committed. The documented sponsor behaviour is mixed and incomplete: there is no documented priming, uptiering or extraction event in the pages read, and there is also no documented equity injection. The 2025 and 2026 transactions added debt service, fixed rent and project commitments faster than they added reported earnings, which is the mechanism behind the going concern note in the latest filing. This view is a fact pack, not a recovery or relative value judgement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The February 7, 2025 merger. Bally’s completed merger transactions with SG Parent LLC and The Queen Casino & Entertainment, Inc., an affiliate of Parent (10-K page:7). Public holders received $18.25 per share in cash, Parent and its affiliates then beneficially owned 73.8% of the common stock, and Queen became a wholly owned subsidiary (Q2-26 10-Q page:8). Share repurchases of 22,804,384 shares for 416,180 thousand in the Successor period to June 30, 2025 equal the number of shares multiplied by $18.25 (Q2-26 10-Q page:4, page:5; calculation below), which is consistent with the cash consideration; I read it as Analyst Interpretation because the filing does not label the repurchase that way in the pages read. Non-cash consideration issued was 955,647 thousand for the company merger and 555,751 thousand for the Queen merger (Q2-26 10-Q page:6). At closing the company issued $500 million of 11% first lien senior secured notes due October 2, 2028 under a note purchase agreement (10-K page:85); the use of proceeds is not stated in the pages read, so whether any distribution was debt-funded is Insufficient Information. The notes were repaid in October 2025: Intralot transaction proceeds first paid down 500.0 million of secured debt pro rata across the 2028 Notes and the Term Loan Facility, then an additional payment of 395.0 million settled the remaining 2028 Notes, with a make-whole payment (10-K page:87).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Intralot transaction. On October 8, 2025 Bally’s completed the transaction under the July 18, 2025 agreement: Intralot paid $1.8 billion in cash and issued about 873.7 million shares for all of Bally’s Holdings Limited, which held the International Interactive business, and Bally’s ownership rose to a controlling 57.9% (Q2-26 10-Q page:8). It was accounted for as an equity transaction with a 42.1% non-controlling interest and no gain or loss (Q2-26 10-Q page:8). Bally’s assumed Intralot debt of about $1.97 billion principal (10-K page:166). Intralot Capital Luxembourg S.A. is the main borrower: a 400.0 million pound term loan, a 200.0 million euro Greek term loan, a super senior revolver with 160.0 million euros of commitments, 600.0 million euros of 6.75% fixed notes and 300.0 million euros of floating notes (Q2-26 10-Q page:31 to page:37). Parent group debt is not guaranteed by Bally’s Intralot, and Bally’s Intralot debt carries its own covenants (a total net leverage ratio not exceeding 4.75:1.00) (Q2-26 10-Q page:11, page:38).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 refinancing and sale-leaseback. On February 11, 2026 the company entered into $1.1 billion of senior secured 2026 Term Loans: Term SOFR (3.0% floor) plus 7.5%, with up to 3.5% payable in kind, secured pari passu with the revolver, due February 11, 2031, or March 1, 2029 if the 2029 Notes remain outstanding on that date (Q2-26 10-Q page:34, page:32). It repaid the previous Term Loan Facility in full, paying $1.48 billion and recognising a $63.4 million loss on extinguishment (Q2-26 10-Q page:33). The same day it sold the Bally’s Twin River land and real estate to GLPI for total consideration of $700.0 million, leased it back under Master Lease No. 2, and agreed 56.0 million of added annual rent; it recorded a gain of $105.8 million (Q2-26 10-Q page:39). Revolver commitments fell by 22.5% to about $519.3 million, with the revolver maturity split into October 2026 and October 2028 tranches and total availability falling to about $319 million from October 2026 (Q2-26 10-Q page:33, page:66). A revolver drawing of $448.0 million made in January 2026 for the New York license fee was repaid in February 2026 (Q2-26 10-Q page:66).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant relief and amendments. In May 2026 the required revolving lenders conditionally waived compliance with the consolidated net leverage ratio covenant from the quarter ended March 31, 2026 until the earlier of the company’s certification election or the day before delivery of the compliance certificate for the quarter ending March 31, 2027; the waiver is conditioned on minimum liquidity, limits on additional secured debt and an agreement to amend the revolver (Q2-26 10-Q page:38). A Fourth Amendment dated May 5, 2026 raised revolver margins (Q2-26 10-Q page:64, page:74); a Fifth Amendment dated July 29, 2026 is listed as incorporated from a Form 8-K of August 5, 2026 whose terms are Not supplied (Q2-26 10-Q page:74). The Q2-26 10-Q states the company does not project that it would satisfy the liquidity maintenance requirement or the reinstated covenant over the next twelve months absent the financings under discussion (page:11).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Development and licence commitments. The company was awarded a New York downstate gaming license in December 2025 and paid the $500.0 million license fee in the first quarter of 2026, plus a $115 million golf course concession contingent payment (Q2-26 10-Q page:44; Q2-26 release page:2). A conveyance arrangement recorded a liability of $183.6 million for specified capital improvements (Q2-26 10-Q page:25), with improvements of approximately $161.0 million required (page:44). The Bronx project is described as a $4.0 billion integrated casino project expected to open by 2030 (Q2-26 release page:2, management language), and a bond or cash deposit equal to 5% of total project investment is required (Q2-26 10-Q page:44). Chicago: the permanent casino targets opening in early 2027 on management’s account (Q2-26 release page:2); GLPI has committed to advance up to $940.0 million of hard costs in exchange for added rent of 8.5% of advances, on top of 20.0 million initial annual rent (Q2-26 10-Q page:70). In the Las Vegas site, the Athletics stadium is slated for completion before the 2028 season (Q2-26 release page:2).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Investments and acquisitions. In April 2025 the company committed A$200 million in convertible notes and subordinated debt for an approximately 38% economic interest in The Star Entertainment Group Limited (10-K page:6); it now holds a 37.7% equity interest (Q2-26 10-Q page:15). Bally’s Intralot agreed in June 2026 to acquire evoke plc, with a cooperation agreement dated June 5, 2026 (Q2-26 release page:1; Q2-26 10-Q page:74). The consideration, financing and approvals timetable are Not supplied; since the buyer is Bally’s Intralot, which does not guarantee parent debt, any financing sits with the Intralot group unless otherwise documented, which is an Analyst Interpretation. Bally’s Intralot also signed a total return equity swap on June 15, 2026 over its own shares for up to 50.0 million euros (Q2-26 10-Q page:28).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent events and new debt after the quarter. Bally’s Intralot, through Intralot Capital, signed a sterling term facilities agreement for 261.8 million pounds on July 27, 2026, drawn in two three-year tranches (Q2-26 10-Q page:37). In July 2026 the company signed a non-binding term sheet for a loan to fund the Bally’s Bronx project and general corporate purposes (Q2-26 10-Q page:11), and in August 2026 a letter of intent with a potential equity investor (Q2-26 release page:2, management language). No later event is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Bally's Corp is a weak, stressed credit whose debt exceeds what its earnings can carry without new financing. Its strongest support is a diversified, licensed operating base that produced Adjusted EBITDA of USD 512.8 million over the last twelve months to June 30, 2026, and a lender group that has granted a conditional covenant waiver. The weakest point is liquidity: debt of USD 4,910.1 million is 9.57x Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest only 1.15x, operations used cash, and the latest filing states substantial doubt about going concern. The outcome will be decided by whether asset sales, an equity sale or new debt close before the waiver conditions and the October 2026 revolver reduction bind, and by what the controlling sponsor does. Nothing after August 14, 2026 is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high on every measure available and rests on a non-GAAP earnings measure. Total debt of USD 4,910.1 million is 9.57x last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 512.8 million, and net of unrestricted cash of USD 390.2 million it is 8.81x [CP-1 leverage chart data]. The ratio rose from 8.88x at September 30, 2025, although the intervening perimeter changes mean it is indicative rather than like-for-like [CP-1 Financial base view]. Operating lease liabilities of USD 2,392.3 million sit outside this debt figure and the fixed rent is deducted inside Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1 financials table].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash earnings are almost fully absorbed by financing and rent. Cash interest of USD 444.6 million is 86.7% of Adjusted EBITDA, so Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 1.15x. Adding the triple net rent expense of USD 210.0 million to cash interest, Adjusted EBITDAR of USD 722.8 million covers the total 1.10x. The 2026 term loans cost at least USD 105.4 million a year even at the 3.0% floor plus the lower 6.5% base-rate margin, and more under the 7.5% Term SOFR margin, and part of the interest may be paid in kind [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 335.7 million over the last twelve months [CP-1 financials table].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the decisive issue. Cash of USD 390.2 million and reported revolver availability of USD 195.8 million total USD 586.0 million, compared with a six-month free cash outflow (operating cash flow less capital expenditures and capitalized software) of USD 359.1 million [CP-1 liquidity chart data; Q2 2026 10-Q page:5]. Revolver commitments are due to fall to about USD 319 million from October 2026 while USD 303.75 million is drawn, which leaves essentially no headroom once the reduction applies, before other usage of USD 19.75 million that CP-1 could not explain [Q2 2026 10-Q page:33]. Whether the reduction occurred, and how it was met, is Not supplied because the pack ends at August 14, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant protection exists only through a conditional waiver. In May 2026 the required lenders conditionally waived the consolidated net leverage ratio covenant for each quarter from March 31, 2026 until the earlier of the company’s election or the day before the compliance certificate for the quarter ending March 31, 2027, subject to minimum liquidity, limits on additional secured debt and an agreement to amend the revolver [Q2 2026 10-Q page:38]. The company states that it does not project that it would satisfy the liquidity maintenance requirement or the reinstated covenant absent the financings under discussion, and that substantial doubt about going concern exists [Q2 2026 10-Q page:11]. The waiver level and the reported ratio are Not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The structure divides the debt across two borrower groups. Parent-group debt is USD 2,898.3 million: USD 1,413.3 million of first lien revolver and 2026 term loans and USD 1,485.0 million of senior notes. Bally’s Intralot debt is USD 2,011.8 million, and Bally’s Intralot does not guarantee the parent’s debt [CP-1 debt table; CP-1A Transaction summary]. The two Intralot-linked segments produced USD 86.7 million of Q2 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDAR, leaving USD 37.4 million of Adjusted EBITDA from casinos, North America Interactive and corporate cost after rent [Q2 2026 10-Q page:48]. The mapping of segments to legal entities is not supplied, so parent-level leverage is only indicative; on this basis it is about 19.4x annualized Q2 2026 and 23.8x last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality is limited by add-backs and by margin pressure. Add-backs for transaction, development, merger, share-based and other items were USD 106.4 million in the six months to June 30, 2026, 43.0% of Adjusted EBITDA of USD 247.3 million [Q2 2026 10-Q page:48]. Q2 2026 revenue rose to USD 792.2 million while Adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 124.0 million from USD 129.2 million, with gaming expenses at 52% of gaming revenue against 43% a year earlier [CP-1 segment base; CP-1A operating model].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Maturities are light until 2029 but the revolver and the 2029 wall matter. Debt maturing through 2027 is USD 141.4 million, 2028 is USD 282.3 million and 2029 is USD 1,007.0 million; the USD 1,109.5 million of 2026 term loans fall due in 2029 instead of 2031 if the 2029 Notes are still outstanding then, which would lift the 2029 amount to USD 2,116.5 million [CP-1 maturities chart data]. Refinancing of the 2029 Notes is therefore linked to the secured term loan maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, Documentary Fact: a diversified, licensed operating base. The company runs 19 US land-based casinos, a large online gaming business and a lottery technology business, with no customer above 10% of revenue, and holds Rhode Island master contracts to 2043, a New York gaming license and a Chicago development [CP-1A Company and operating model; Company profile]. This supports revenue durability, although segment cash earnings are not evenly distributed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, Documentary Fact: lender engagement and external funding for part of the capital programme. Lenders granted a waiver and amended the revolver in 2026, and GLPI has committed to advance up to USD 940.0 million for Chicago construction, which reduces the company’s own capital need there [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Lender engagement lowers near-term acceleration risk but does not remove the conditions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, Documentary Fact: contained near-term amortisation. Remaining 2026 and 2027 maturities total USD 141.4 million, and a parent revolver default has no implications under Bally’s Intralot’s debt documents [CP-1 maturities chart data; Q2 2026 10-Q page:11]. This limits contagion from a parent-level default to the Intralot group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, Analyst Interpretation: real estate and asset monetisation capacity. The Bally’s Twin River sale-leaseback realised USD 700.0 million of consideration, and the company lists asset monetisation among its plans [CP-1A Transaction summary]. This is also a weakness because each sale adds fixed rent, so I count it only as a source of liquidity, not of lower fixed charges.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, Documentary Fact: leverage and cover. Gross leverage of 9.57x, net leverage of 8.81x and cover of 1.15x leave little cushion, and the fixed-charge cover including rent is 1.10x [CP-1 charts; calculations below].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, Documentary Fact: liquidity and going concern. Operating cash flow is negative, cash fell from USD 798.4 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 390.2 million at June 30, 2026, and the latest filing states substantial doubt [CP-1 liquidity chart data; CP-1A Company profile].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, Analyst Interpretation: structure and control. A controlling sponsor holds 67.1%, no equity support is documented, parent creditors rank behind Intralot creditors at the Intralot level, and 42.1% of Intralot equity belongs to others [CP-1A Company profile; Governance]. The sponsor’s response is the key unknown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, Documentary Fact: reporting quality and regulation. The 10-K reports an adverse opinion on internal control because of a material weakness, results were first issued as preliminary, and the Rhode Island regulatory agreement restricts payments and debt incurrence above a 5.50 to 1.00 leverage trigger whose definition and status are not supplied [CP-1A Company profile].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, Documentary Fact: uncommitted large projects. The USD 4.0 billion Bally’s Bronx project has a non-binding loan term sheet and a letter of intent with a potential equity investor, and construction at Chicago continues [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Funding competes with debt service.
